name: watersplash-clippath

frames.best_why: Both splash cut-outs and their photos are fully visible, with the droplets and edges clear.

tagline: Two photos shaped like splashing paint on a black stage.
summary: A pair of photos each clipped to an inky water-splash silhouette: a blue city skyline on the left and a yellow-toned landscape with a building on the right, both on black.
appearance: Two images sit side by side on black, each cut to a ragged ink-splash outline with round droplets flung out around it. Left is a cool blue cityscape of glass towers; right is a warm yellow and olive view of a building and field.
behaviour: Pointing at either splash scales the picture up inside the fixed cut-out, cropping it tighter while the splash silhouette holds its shape.
demo_content: A blue skyscraper city and a yellow building landscape.
use_when: A creative page needs two images with a bold ink-splash crop instead of plain rectangles.
avoid_when: The clip paths are fixed SVG shapes and both photos are hardcoded, so fitting new images needs editing.
customise: Two image URLs are hardcoded and each figure points at a specific splash clip-path id; changing pictures or shapes means editing the source and defs.
weight_why: Two images and a CSS scale transition; nothing runs at rest.

a11y.note: Both photos use empty alt text, so the city and landscape are undescribed, and the hover scale ignores prefers-reduced-motion.

issues: Both images have empty alt text.
The splash clip paths are fixed to two images, so other aspect ratios can crop badly.
polish_why: Bold splash silhouettes and strong image pairing; empty alt text and fixed crops hold it back.
title: Water Splash Clip Path
